title: Remediations run frequently against large populations

largePopulation.text: Devices above which frequency has a measurable cost

maxFrequencyHours.text: Interval below which frequency starts to matter

report.title: {Items.Count} {Plural(Items.Count, 'remediation runs', 'remediations run')} hourly on a large population

messages.businessImpact: Every run costs processor time on every device and generates reporting traffic. At this scale it is a measurable drain for a check that rarely finds anything.
remediation: Reduce the frequency to daily unless the condition genuinely recurs within hours.
messages.cannotSee: What the script costs to run is not measured, only how often it runs and how many devices it runs on. A detection script that reads one registry value hourly costs almost nothing; one that walks a disk costs a great deal, and they read the same here. Where a remediation is assigned to several groups the shortest schedule is taken, because that is the one setting the cost, and a remediation set to run once has no interval and is passed over.
